summary: Appends a copy of an item to a linked list owned by `this`. Allocates a 332-byte payload, initializes its back-pointer to the list owner plus a zero/-1 dword pair, copies 0x140 bytes of item data from a2 into the payload, optionally reallocates a3's string buffer (result discarded), then wraps the payload in a 12-byte node (payload pointer, next pointer, valid flag = 1) and links it at the tail of the list, updating head/tail pointers and the count at this+0xC. Always returns 0. Called by sub_565F80.

operations.description: If the item pointer a2 is null, skip the whole insertion and return 0.
Allocate a 332-byte payload object via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper; on failure v3 remains null.
If allocation succeeded, initialize the payload: store the owning list pointer `this` at byte offset 0, zero the dword at byte offset 324 (payload[81]), and set -1 at byte offset 328 (payload[82]).
Copy 0x140 bytes from a2 into the payload at byte offset 4 (payload + 1) via qmemcpy.
If a3 is nonzero, call StringCopyWithBufferRealloc(a3) for its side effect (string buffer reallocation); the return value is discarded.
Allocate a 12-byte list node via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper; on failure v6 is null.
If the node allocated, initialize it: payload pointer at byte offset 0, next pointer at byte offset 4 set to 0, and valid-flag byte at byte offset 8 set to 1.
If the list head at this+0x0 is null (empty list), set the head (this+0x0), the this+0x8 pointer, and the tail (this+0x4) all to the new node, then increment the count at this+0xC.

Otherwise append to the tail: write the new node as the next pointer of the old tail (this+0x4 dereferenced at byte offset 4), set the tail this+0x4 to the new node, and increment the count at this+0xC.

clean_pseudocode: payload[0] = this;   // back-pointer to owning list
this[0] = node; this[2] = node; this[1] = node;
